 After midnight
 Phone on or phone off, you lose either way 
 1 Awake for nothing
 Out-of-hours calls wake you for jobs that could wait. Turn the phone off and you lose the call-out that pays best.
 2 The job that went elsewhere
 A customer with no power rings until somebody picks up. If that is not you, the job and any follow-on rewire go elsewhere.
 3 You decide what wakes you
 You decide what counts as urgent. Genuine emergencies reach you straight away. Everything else is logged for the morning, so you can sleep.
 Three piles
 How it sorts a call 
 Each column is set with you before it answers anybody, and any of them can be changed afterwards.
 Wake me now
 Whatever you say is a genuine emergency, such as a total loss of power or a fault that cannot wait. It reaches you straight away.
 Tell me in the morning
 An EICR quote, an extra socket or a price for a new consumer unit. Logged with the details and ready when your day starts.
 Not for us
 Sales calls, jobs outside your patch and work you do not take. The caller gets a polite answer, and you stay asleep.
 Safety comes first. A caller reporting burning smells, sparking or danger is told to leave the property and call 999, or the network operator on 105 for a power cut.
 Cost
 What call-out cover costs to put in place 
 Setup starts at £497, followed by a monthly fee from £97. The rules it follows go in your written scope first, so the price and the job are agreed together.

 Set-up
 Your rules first, then your phone 
 01 Set what wakes you
 Go through your out-of-hours work with Andy and decide what is urgent, what can wait and what you never take.
 02 Hear it handle a fault
 Ring it as a worried customer would. It tells you it is an AI, asks your questions, and you say what to change.
 03 Hand over the night phone
 Calls go to it at the times you choose. Emergencies come through, and the rest waits for you after breakfast.

 Call-out questions
 What electricians want pinned down first 
 How does it decide what is urgent?
 By following the rules you set with Andy and asking the questions you have chosen. When the answers match what you have called urgent, it reaches you straight away. You also decide in advance which way it should lean when it is unsure.
 What does it tell someone in danger?
 Anyone reporting burning smells, sparking or danger is told to leave the property and call 999, or the network operator on 105 for a power cut. It gives no electrical advice and makes no attempt to diagnose the fault.
 Can it take my out-of-hours rates?
 Yes, if you want callers to hear them. Give Andy your call-out rates and the hours they apply, and it can state them as given. If you would sooner quote yourself, it says the price will be confirmed.
 Do I still get the routine enquiries?
 Yes. Routine work is logged with its details and kept for the morning, so none of it disappears because it came in at night.
 How is this different from aiforelectricians.co.uk?
 aiforelectricians.co.uk looks at AI and automation across a whole electrical business. This site deals with one thing only, which is emergency and out-of-hours call-outs.
 Is it an answering service for electricians?
 It does what an electrician answering service would, then adds the sorting by your rules. Some people would call it an AI receptionist for electricians. Whatever the name, callers are told it is an AI.

 About this call-out service
 AI Voice Agents for Electricians is a service from Antek Automation, the sole trader based in Andover and led by Andy Norman. It is for electricians who take emergency and out-of-hours work anywhere in the UK. The technology is explained further at Antek's AI voice agents hub .

 He starts with what should wake you up. Everything else about the build follows from that answer, including what it says to a caller in danger.
